mechanism_narrative: Declining TRANSIT mobility over the past four weeks (from +3.3% to -8.7%) signals reduced commuting and public movement. This sustained transit contraction directly suppresses retail foot traffic, as fewer people in transit hubs and commute corridors translates to lower retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined 12 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -5% in the first two weeks of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (from +4.9% to +9.3%) indicates people spending more time at home, reflecting either voluntary isolation or restriction compliance. This behavioral shift away from out-of-home activity directly reduces retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks as home-based time crowds out retail visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased 4.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in the first two weeks of the forecast period while RESIDENTIAL remains above +8%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -14.9% at t-2w to +6.0% at t-1w and -0.6% at t-0w, signaling volatile workplace attendance. When WORKPLACES stabilizes above -5%, commuter-driven retail activity rebounds within one week as office workers resume shopping during commute windows and lunch breaks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -5% for one consecutive week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in week t+1w is lower than the mean of the last four weeks despite WORKPLACES being above -5% in week t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains persistently elevated (48.6–53.7%) while RETAIL_REC has collapsed to -13.3%, indicating consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. This bifurcation reflects risk-averse behavior where essential trips displace recreational mobility. Retail recovery requires GROCERY_PHARM to fall below 45%, signaling normalization of essential-shopping urgency.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM-to-RETAIL_REC spread is 62.2 percentage points at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45% throughout the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply from -4.4% to -16.7% over four weeks, indicating suppressed outdoor leisure activity. This sustained parks contraction signals broader outdoor-activity aversion that extends to outdoor retail venues and shopping districts. Retail recovery requires PARKS to rebound above -10%, indicating renewed outdoor mobility appetite.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 12.3 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in weeks t+1w and t+2w both exceed the t-0w value of -13.3% while PARKS remains below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous contraction in TRANSIT (-8.7%), WORKPLACES (-0.6%), and PARKS (-16.7%) at t-0w indicates active mobility restrictions or lockdown conditions. Under such regime, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed unless all three series rebound above their respective t-3w baselines within two weeks, signaling policy relaxation.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -5% AND PARKS < -10% AND WORKPLACES < 0% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:All three series negative or near-zero at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -5% in week t+1w or t+2w while the trigger condition (all three series in contraction) remains active.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has increased 4.4 percentage points over four weeks to +9.3%, consistent with seasonal holiday or festive-period behavior in mid-January. This seasonal home-concentration effect suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility as consumers substitute home-based leisure for out-of-home shopping. The effect persists for four weeks unless RESIDENTIAL falls below +5%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +7% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is +9.3%, highest in the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +7% for all four weeks of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery from -14.9% to +6.0% combined with TRANSIT stabilization above -5% at t-0w signals restoration of commuting routines. This two-proxy convergence triggers retail recovery within one week as office workers resume shopping patterns. The mechanism fails if WORKPLACES falls below 0% in week t+1w, indicating renewed workplace disruption.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at t-1w is +6.0%, TRANSIT at t-0w is -8.7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in week t+1w is lower than the mean of weeks t-3w through t-0w despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT meeting the trigger condition in week t-0w.
